title: A Bronx Tale
tagline: Nobody on this street leaves a plate half eaten.
about: A bus driver's son is torn between his honest father and the neighbourhood boss.
cue: Do the car door test before dessert comes out.
faces: Summer night on 187th. The light stays on.
Eat, have a drink, leave the dice alone.
Good one hour from time punched.

    StartersFried stuffed olivesBig green olives packed with sharp provolone, crackling crumb, lemon garlic mayonnaise, a pinch of chilli.From the bar at Chez Bippy. Kitchen till midnight.How to make it24 large pitted green olives80g sharp provolone40g plain flour1 egg80g fine breadcrumbs500ml neutral oil, for frying1/2 lemon, zested and juiced1 garlic clove, crushed100g mayonnaisechilli flakes, to dustDrain the olives and pat dry. Cut the provolone into small sticks and push one into each olive.Roll in flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.Stir the lemon zest, juice and garlic into the mayonnaise to make the aioli.Heat the oil to 180°C and fry in two batches until deep golden, then drain.Dust with chilli flakes and serve with the aioli.Garlic knotsHot from the oven, brushed with butter, parsley and grated parmesan.For a warm night on the stoop.How to make it400g pizza dough50g butter2 garlic cloves, minced2 tbsp chopped parsley30g parmesan, finely gratedCut the dough into 12 strips and tie each in a loose knot.Place on a lined tray, cover and prove in a warm place for 30 minutes.Bake at 230°C for 12 minutes until golden.Melt the butter with the garlic over low heat for 2 minutes.Toss the hot knots with the garlic butter, parsley and parmesan.MainsSonny's Sunday rigatoniSlow tomato gravy, pork and beef meatballs, tender ribs, torn basil.Ask for the JoJo portion.How to make it400g pork and beef mince1 egg40g breadcrumbs1 tsp salt1/4 tsp black pepper400g pork ribs2 tbsp olive oil1 onion, diced3 garlic cloves, sliced800g tinned tomatoes200ml water10 basil leaves400g rigatoniMix the mince with egg, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper and shape into 12 meatballs.Brown the meatballs and ribs in olive oil in a heavy pot, turning, then set aside.Soften the onion, add the garlic, then the tomatoes, water and basil.Return the meat, cover partly and simmer gently, stirring and adding water if needed. Check the ribs are tender and the meatballs cooked through.Boil the rigatoni, drain and toss with the sauce. Serve the meat on a platter.SweetsBelmont cannoliCrisp shells piped to order, vanilla ricotta, chocolate chips, pistachio.Every Sunday, one sitting.How to make it250g fresh ricotta40g icing sugar1/2 tsp vanilla extract30g mini chocolate chips8 small cannoli shells30g pistachios, finely crushedDrain the ricotta in a lined sieve in the fridge for at least 2 hours.Beat with icing sugar and vanilla until smooth, then fold in the chocolate chips.Pipe into the shells just before serving.Dip the ends in crushed pistachios. Serve two per person.DrinksEspresso & anisetteShort black coffee, anisette or sambuca on the side, lemon peel.A1 on the jukebox corner.How to make it36g espresso beans60ml anisette or sambuca1 lemonBrew four short espressos into warmed demitasse cups.Cut four small curls of lemon peel, avoiding the white pith.Serve the anisette beside each cup for pouring in, with a lemon curl.
